STARS = "*\u2217"


class ImkError(RuntimeError):
    """A meta-analysis table cannot be read as expected."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Stats:
    """One column of a descriptive table."""

    column: str
    document: str
    mean: float
    median: float
    sd: float
    maximum: float
    minimum: float
    n: int

    @property
    def coefficient_of_variation(self) -> float:
        """Dispersion relative to the central value.

        The honest summary of these tables: for tax-side multipliers the standard
        deviation EXCEEDS the mean. That is the property the L4 banner is describing,
        and it is stronger than the "facteur 3 à 5" the copy proposes.
        """
        if self.mean == 0:
            raise ImkError(f"{self.column}: a mean of zero has no coefficient of variation")
        return abs(self.sd / self.mean)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RegimeEffect:
    """One regime coefficient from the meta-regression, with its standard error."""

    regime: str
    coefficient: float
    standard_error: float
    stars: int
    """Significance as printed: 3 for ***, 2 for **, 1 for *, 0 for none. RUP prints
    none in the base specification, which is the finding — there is no measured
    upswing effect to build a ratio on."""

    @property
    def significant(self) -> bool:
        return self.stars >= 2


def regime_effect(raw: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, RegimeEffect]:
    """The controlled regime coefficients of WP139, Table 4, base specification.

    Additive units of multiplier, not a ratio. `regime_effect()["RLO"].coefficient` is
    how much a DOWNTURN adds to a spending multiplier, all else controlled.
    """
    path = (raw or RAW) / DOCUMENTS["wp139"]
    if not path.exists():
        raise ImkError(f"{path} not found — download it and record it in the manifest "
                       f"(`impots data fetch {path.name}`)")
    text = " ".join(_lines(str(path))[:])
    found: dict[str, RegimeEffect] = {}
    for regime in REGIME_ROWS:
        # "RLO 0.769(0.143)***0.653(0.126)***..." — the first pair is column (1), the
        # base specification the paper calls best practice. The stars extract as U+2217
        # ASTERISK OPERATOR, not ASCII: matching only "*" silently reads every
        # coefficient as non-significant, which inverts this row's whole finding.
        match = re.search(
            rf"{regime}\s+(-?\d+\.\d+)\s*\(\s*(\d+\.\d+)\s*\)\s*([{STARS}]*)", text)
        if match is None:
            raise ImkError(
                f"regime coefficient {regime!r} not found in table 4. The paper may "
                f"have been revised — do not fall back to the raw subsample means, "
                f"which are what this function exists to replace."
            )
        found[regime] = RegimeEffect(
            regime=regime, coefficient=float(match.group(1)),
            standard_error=float(match.group(2)), stars=len(match.group(3)),
        )
    return found


def _normalise(line: str) -> str:
    # The extractor renders the fi/fl ligatures as single codepoints.
    return " ".join(line.replace("ﬁ", "fi").replace("ﬂ", "fl").split())


def _floats(tail: str) -> list[float]:
    return [float(v) for v in re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", tail)]


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _lines(path: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    import pypdf

    return tuple(
        _normalise(line)
        for page in pypdf.PdfReader(path).pages
        for line in (page.extract_text() or "").splitlines()
    )


def load(document: str, raw: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, Stats]:
    """Every descriptive-statistics column of one meta-analysis.

    Raises rather than returning a partial table: a block silently lost to a spelling
    variant would leave a column missing, and a caller asking for it would get a
    KeyError far from the cause.
    """
    if document not in DOCUMENTS:
        raise ImkError(f"unknown document {document!r}; have {sorted(DOCUMENTS)}")
    path = (raw or RAW) / DOCUMENTS[document]
    if not path.exists():
        raise ImkError(f"{path} not found — download it and record it in the manifest "
                       f"(`impots data fetch {path.name}`)")
    if importlib.util.find_spec("pypdf") is None:  # pragma: no cover - environment
        raise ImkError("pypdf is required to read the IMK working papers")

    known = COLUMNS[document]
    stats: dict[str, Stats] = {}
    lines = _lines(str(path))
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        tokens = line.split()
        if len(tokens) < 3 or not all(token in known for token in tokens):
            continue
        block = _block(lines[index + 1: index + 12], tokens, document)
        # Later blocks repeat no column, so a duplicate means the header matched
        # something that was not a header.
        for column, values in block.items():
            stats.setdefault(column, values)
    missing = known - set(stats)
    if missing:
        raise ImkError(
            f"{document}: no descriptive block found for {sorted(missing)}. The paper "
            f"may have been revised — do not fall back to a neighbouring column."
        )
    return stats


def _block(following: tuple[str, ...], columns: list[str], document: str) -> dict[str, Stats]:
    rows: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    for line in following:
        for key, labels in STAT_LABELS.items():
            label = next((lab for lab in labels if line.startswith(lab)), None)
            if label is None or key in rows:
                continue
            values = _floats(line[len(label):])
            if len(values) == len(columns):
                rows[key] = values
    if set(rows) != set(STAT_LABELS):
        return {}
    return {
        column: Stats(
            column=column, document=document,
            mean=rows["mean"][i], median=rows["median"][i], sd=rows["sd"][i],
            maximum=rows["maximum"][i], minimum=rows["minimum"][i], n=int(rows["n"][i]),
        )
        for i, column in enumerate(columns)
    }


#: These tables have no horizon dimension at all: a meta-analysis pools estimates made
#: at whatever horizon each primary study chose. Saying so with an explicit single
#: "all" is better than inventing years the source does not carry.
HORIZONS = ("all",)


def table(row: str, document: str = "wp117",
          raw: Path | None = None) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[float, ...]], tuple[str, ...]]:
    """One statistic across every column, as (values by column, horizons).

    `row` names an attribute of `Stats`, so a derived quantity like
    `coefficient_of_variation` is addressable without being stored — it is computed by
    the same reviewed code that parsed the table it comes from.
    """
    stats = load(document, raw=raw)
    try:
        return {column: (float(getattr(value, row)),) for column, value in stats.items()}, HORIZONS
    except AttributeError as error:
        raise ImkError(
            f"{document}: no statistic {row!r} on a descriptive column; "
            f"have mean, median, sd, maximum, minimum, n, coefficient_of_variation"
        ) from error
fichiers.impots/macro/io_layer.py:
"""B2 — composition and leakage from the input-output table (PHASE4_SPEC §1).

**This module returns shares and fractions. It never returns a level.** That is the
whole design, and the reason is the anti-double-counting rule §1 opens with: the
literature's fiscal multipliers already contain input-output propagation and induced
effects. Running an impulse through a Leontief inverse *and* multiplying the result by
a literature multiplier counts the same propagation twice.

So the two mechanisms have disjoint jobs, and the split runs exactly along
shape-versus-size:

* the **multiplier** decides how big the macro response is;
* the **table** decides which branches it lands in, and how much of it leaks abroad
  before it can land anywhere.

Every public function here therefore returns something dimensionless. A function that
returned euros of output would be an invitation to add it to the aggregate path, and
`first_round_shares` sums to one by construction rather than by convention.

**Type I, and the assertion the spec asked for.** The coefficient matrix is the
branch × branch block alone: households stay exogenous, so the inverse propagates
inter-industry demand and nothing else. Closing the model on household income — the
Type II inverse — would add the induced consumption round, which is precisely the round
the literature multiplier already contains. `assert_type_one` states it, and
`test_type_two_would_double_count` measures how much it would have added.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from impots.macro.tes import Tes

#: Below this, an impulse is numerically indistinguishable from no impulse and its
#: composition is meaningless rather than merely uncertain.
MINIMUM_IMPULSE_EUR = 1.0


class IoLayerError(RuntimeError):
    """The input-output layer was asked for something it must not provide."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Composition:
    """The shape of a first-round shock. Dimensionless throughout."""

    branches: tuple[str, ...]
    output_shares: np.ndarray
    """Share of first-round domestic output by branch. Sums to 1."""
    employment_shares: np.ndarray
    """Share of the first-round employment content by branch. Sums to 1."""
    persons_per_million_eur: float
    """Employment intensity of *this* impulse's mix, in persons per million euros of
    domestic output. A property of the composition, not a forecast: multiplied by a
    level it would produce jobs, which is B3's business, not B2's.

    Persons, not thousands. The accounts publish thousands and the arithmetic runs in
    them, but a coefficient near 0.005 invites a factor-of-a-thousand error at every
    later use, so the unit is converted once, here, where it can be tested."""
    leakage: float
    """Imports induced per euro of impulse, in [0, 1). Both channels: product bought
    directly from abroad to meet the final demand, and the imported input content of
    the domestic production the rest of it sets off. The correction §1 requires to be
    computed rather than assumed."""
    direct_leakage: float
    """The first channel alone, kept separate because it is the one a reader can check
    against the published import table."""
    vintage: str
    base_year: int

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        for name in ("output_shares", "employment_shares"):
            shares = getattr(self, name)
            if not np.isclose(shares.sum(), 1.0, atol=1e-9):
                raise IoLayerError(f"{name} sums to {shares.sum()}, not 1")
        if not 0.0 <= self.leakage < 1.0:
            raise IoLayerError(f"leakage {self.leakage} is not a fraction")

    @property
    def domestic_share(self) -> float:
        """What survives leakage — the factor B3 applies to the aggregate impulse."""
        return 1.0 - self.leakage


def technical_coefficients(tes: Tes) -> np.ndarray:
    """A, the domestic input-output coefficient matrix.

    Branch × branch only. The published table carries one negative cell (the SIFIM
    adjustment, D-048), which is kept: clamping it would break a balance identity that
    closes exactly, and the properties propagation needs survive it.
    """
    output = tes.total_output
    if (output <= 0).any():
        zero = [tes.branches[i] for i, v in enumerate(output) if v <= 0]
        raise IoLayerError(f"branches with non-positive output cannot be inverted: {zero}")
    return tes.domestic / output


def leontief_inverse(coefficients: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """(I - A)^-1, the Type I inverse.

    Type I because households are exogenous: the branch × branch block propagates
    inter-industry demand and stops. The induced consumption round belongs to the
    literature multiplier and adding it here would count it twice.
    """
    radius = float(np.max(np.abs(np.linalg.eigvals(coefficients))))
    if radius >= 1.0:
        raise IoLayerError(
            f"spectral radius {radius:.4f} >= 1: a unit of demand would generate "
            f"unbounded output, and the inverse does not converge"
        )
    return np.linalg.inv(np.eye(len(coefficients)) - coefficients)


def assert_type_one(coefficients: np.ndarray, tes: Tes) -> None:
    """The coefficient matrix must be the branch block and nothing more.

    §1's sentence — "the induced round belongs to the multiplier and must not be added
    here" — as a check rather than a comment. A Type II matrix is square in n+1, with a
    household row and column closing income onto consumption; this refuses one.
    """
    if coefficients.shape != (tes.n, tes.n):
        raise IoLayerError(
            f"coefficients are {coefficients.shape}, not ({tes.n}, {tes.n}). A closed "
            f"(Type II) matrix adds the induced consumption round, which the literature "
            f"multiplier already contains — that is double counting, not more realism."
        )


def import_share_of_final_use(tes: Tes, use: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Share of each product's final demand met by imports rather than domestic output.

    This is the direct channel, and reading only the domestic sheet makes it invisible:
    9.1 % of final consumption and 14.8 % of fixed capital formation are imported
    product, bought as such. An impulse routed entirely through the domestic Leontief
    would credit French branches with output that is in fact bought abroad.
    """
    if use not in tes.final_uses or use not in tes.imported_final_uses:
        raise IoLayerError(f"unknown final-use category {use!r}; have {sorted(tes.final_uses)}")
    domestic, imported = tes.final_uses[use], tes.imported_final_uses[use]
    total = domestic + imported
    # A product with no final use of this kind gets no split rather than a divide by
    # zero; nothing is allocated to it anyway.
    return np.where(total > 0, imported / np.where(total > 0, total, 1.0), 0.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)


def split_demand(tes: Tes, demand: np.ndarray, use: str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """(demand met domestically, demand met directly by imports)."""
    share = import_share_of_final_use(tes, use)
    direct = demand * share
    return demand - direct, direct


def leakage(tes: Tes, demand: np.ndarray,
            use: str = "total_emplois_finals") -> tuple[float, float]:
    """(total leakage, direct leakage) per euro of impulse.

    Total is imports induced per euro of impulse — the fraction that never reaches a
    French producer, through either channel. The denominator is the impulse itself, not
    gross output: gross output double-counts inter-industry sales and would make the
    ratio depend on how vertically integrated the affected branches happen to be.
    """
    total_impulse = float(demand.sum())
    if total_impulse <= 0:
        raise IoLayerError("an impulse of zero or less has no import content")
    domestic_demand, direct = split_demand(tes, demand, use)
    output = first_round_output(tes, domestic_demand)
    input_coefficients = tes.imported.sum(axis=0) / tes.total_output
    indirect = float((input_coefficients * output).sum())
    return (float(direct.sum()) + indirect) / total_impulse, float(direct.sum()) / total_impulse


def first_round_output(tes: Tes, demand: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Domestic output by branch generated by a final-demand vector, Type I.

    Internal: the level it returns is in the units of `demand`, and letting it out of
    the module is how the aggregate path would come to be counted twice. Public callers
    get `composition`, which normalises it.
    """
    if demand.shape != (tes.n,):
        raise IoLayerError(f"demand is {demand.shape}, expected ({tes.n},)")
    if (demand < 0).any():
        raise IoLayerError(
            "a negative final-demand component makes the composition shares meaningless; "
            "split a mixed impulse into its expansionary and contractionary parts and "
            "compose each"
        )
    coefficients = technical_coefficients(tes)
    assert_type_one(coefficients, tes)
    return leontief_inverse(coefficients) @ demand


def composition(tes: Tes, demand: np.ndarray, jobs: np.ndarray,
                use: str = "total_emplois_finals") -> Composition:
    """The shape of a first-round shock: where it lands, and what leaks.

    `demand` is TOTAL final demand by product — domestic and imported together, as a
    reform's spending impulse arrives — in any consistent unit; the result is
    dimensionless, so the unit cancels and is deliberately not recorded. `use` names
    which published category supplies the domestic/import split, since consumption and
    capital formation do not import in the same proportion. `jobs` is employment by
    branch in thousands, ordered to match, from the same accounts vintage.
    """
    if demand.shape != (tes.n,):
        raise IoLayerError(f"demand is {demand.shape}, expected ({tes.n},)")
    total = float(demand.sum())
    if total < MINIMUM_IMPULSE_EUR:
        raise IoLayerError(
            f"impulse of {total} is below {MINIMUM_IMPULSE_EUR}: its composition would "
            f"be numerical noise, not a small effect"
        )
    if jobs.shape != (tes.n,):
        raise IoLayerError(f"employment is {jobs.shape}, expected ({tes.n},)")

    domestic_demand, _ = split_demand(tes, demand, use)
    output = first_round_output(tes, domestic_demand)
    intensity = jobs / tes.total_output          # thousands of persons per M EUR
    employment = output * intensity
    total_leakage, direct = leakage(tes, demand, use)
    return Composition(
        branches=tes.branches,
        output_shares=output / output.sum(),
        employment_shares=employment / employment.sum(),
        persons_per_million_eur=float(employment.sum() / output.sum()) * 1_000.0,
        leakage=total_leakage,
        direct_leakage=direct,
        vintage=tes.vintage,
        base_year=tes.base_year,
    )
fichiers.impots/macro/mesange.py:
"""Reading the Mésange variant tables (M1).

Mésange is the quarterly macroeconometric model of the French economy maintained
jointly by INSEE and the DG Trésor. Its section 4, "Principales variantes", publishes
the response of the economy to a 1-point-of-GDP shock on each budgetary instrument,
at 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 years and in the long run — GDP, employment, consumption,
household income and the primary balance.

That is the multiplier evidence this project needs, from an official French source,
instrument by instrument, with the horizon profile attached rather than assumed.

**The numbers are parsed from the PDF, never transcribed.** D-026: calibration inputs
are computed from the primary file by tested code, because a figure that passes through
a human's or an agent's retyping has been measured twice failing. The YAML alongside
carries scope, support and verdicts — never a value.

One property of the source that must travel with every number it yields: Mésange is a
**linear** model. It has no cycle state, so it cannot answer what a multiplier becomes
in a slump, and the sign conventions below assume a symmetry the model imposes by
construction rather than one anybody measured.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

RAW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "data" / "raw"

SOURCE_FILE = "insee_G2017-04_mesange.pdf"

#: Horizons, in the column order the tables print them. "LT" is the model's long-run
#: equilibrium, not a year, and is kept under its own name rather than given a number.
HORIZONS = ("1", "2", "3", "5", "10", "LT")

#: The rows worth reading, keyed by the label each table prints in its left column.
ROWS = {
    "gdp": "PIB en volume",
    "consommation": "Consommation des ménages",
    "investissement_entreprises": "Investissement des SNF et EI",
    "revenu_disponible": "Revenu disponible réel des ménages",
    "emploi_milliers": "Emploi salarié marchand (en milliers)",
    "solde_primaire_pts_pib": "Solde primaire des APU (en pts de PIB)",
}

#: Row labels the ordinary variant tables print. The targeted variant overrides them:
#: it prints "PIB (en volume et en %)" and carries no price or balance rows at all.
ROWS_TARGETED = {
    "gdp": "PIB (en volume et en %)",
    "emploi_milliers": "Emploi salarié marchand (en milliers)",
    "emploi_qualifie": "Emploi qualifié",
    "emploi_non_qualifie": "Emploi non qualifié",
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VariantSpec:
    """How to find one variant, and what the document says its shock actually is.

    Each field here exists because the adversarial pass found the row claiming
    otherwise. They are not decoration: `ex_ante_points` and `basis` change the
    arithmetic, and `targeted` decides which reforms may use the row at all.
    """

    shock: str
    """The sentence printed above the table, verbatim. Variants are addressed by it
    rather than by section number, since the heading sometimes resolves to the block
    title. NOT unique in the document — "Hausse de l'investissement public de 1 % du
    PIB en volume" also appears on p52 and p136 — so the reader additionally requires
    every expected row on the same page and keeps the first qualifying page."""

    expansionary_sign: int
    """+1 if published as an expansionary shock, -1 if published contractionary and
    flipped. The flip assumes symmetry. The document is CONSISTENT with additivity
    between instruments without proving it (D-230): encadré 15, the "TVA sociale"
    composite, matches the sum of the VAT and employer-contribution variants to within
    one unit of the last printed digit — not "to the centime": six cells differ by one
    unit, in GDP, consumption, employment, the primary balance and the CPI — which is
    what adding the two tables would give too, and the document does not say the box
    was run on its own. No table runs a variant in both directions, so symmetry
    remains an unmeasured assumption."""

    basis: str
    """"ex_ante_fiscal" or "volume". p101 reserves the ex ante convention: "les
    variantes FISCALES sont effectuées à hauteur de 1 % du PIB ex ante, soit un montant
    de 22 Md€ en 2015". The two spending variants are shocks in VOLUME, so calling them
    ex ante — as this file did until the verification — mis-states three lines of eight."""

    ex_ante_points: float = 1.0
    """Points of GDP the shock actually costs ex ante. 1.0 everywhere except VAT, where
    p113 prints: "Considérant que les APU versent environ 15 % du total des recettes de
    TVA, le choc s'élève à 1,18 point de PIB ex ante pour atteindre effectivement 1
    point de PIB de recettes de TVA supplémentaires en termes nets." A VAT reform costed
    GROSS ex ante — the usual PLF convention — would otherwise receive a multiplier
    overstated by 18 %."""

    targeted: bool = False
    """True only for the low-wage variant of encadré 14. The eight main variants are
    UNIFORM: p118 "il n'existe dans le modèle qu'un unique taux d'imposition sur le
    revenu identique pour l'ensemble des salariés"; p108 a "baisse uniforme de 3,7
    points". Routing a low-wage allègement to a uniform variant understates employment
    by 39 % at three years."""

    rows: dict[str, str] | None = None
    caveat: str = ""


#: The published variants. `expansionary_sign` brings them all to one convention: GDP
#: response per point of GDP of expansionary impulse.
VARIANTS: dict[str, VariantSpec] = {
    "investissement_public": VariantSpec(
        "Hausse de l’investissement public de 1 % du PIB en volume", +1, "volume",
        caveat="Réparti au prorata de la composition moyenne de l'investissement public "
               "(61 % services abrités, 27 % services exposés, 11 % biens manufacturés), "
               "dont dépend le contenu en imports."),
    "depense_publique": VariantSpec(
        "Hausse de la dépense publique d’un montant de 1 point de PIB", +1, "volume",
        caveat="COMPOSITE, et non un instrument : 8 % investissement public, 25 % "
               "rémunérations publiques, 9 % prestations en nature, 12 % consommations "
               "intermédiaires, 46 % PRESTATIONS SOCIALES EN ESPÈCES (p106). Contient "
               "donc 8 % de la variante investissement public — les additionner double "
               "compte. Son emploi LT (-42 000 marchand) s'accompagne d'une HAUSSE de "
               "l'emploi total de 26 000 y compris public (p107) : rapporter le premier "
               "seul inverse la conclusion."),
    "cotisations_employeurs": VariantSpec(
        "Baisse des cotisations sociales employeurs de 1 % du PIB ex ante", +1,
        "ex_ante_fiscal",
        caveat="Baisse UNIFORME de 3,7 points, portant à 80 % sur des salariés qualifiés. "
               "Pour un allègement ciblé bas salaires, utiliser "
               "`cotisations_employeurs_ciblees`."),
    "cotisations_salaries": VariantSpec(
        "Baisse des cotisations sociales salariés de 1 % du PIB ex ante", +1,
        "ex_ante_fiscal",
        caveat="Baisse uniforme de 3,7 points sur un taux d'un peu plus de 13 %."),
    "tva": VariantSpec(
        "Hausse de la TVA de 1 % du PIB ex ante", -1, "ex_ante_fiscal",
        ex_ante_points=1.18,
        caveat="Le choc est de 1,18 point de PIB ex ante pour 1 point net, les APU "
               "versant ~15 % de la TVA."),
    "csg": VariantSpec(
        "Baisse de la contribution sociale généralisée de 1 % du PIB ex ante", +1,
        "ex_ante_fiscal"),
    "impot_sur_le_revenu": VariantSpec(
        "Baisse de l’impôt sur le revenu des ménages de 1 % du PIB ex ante", +1,
        "ex_ante_fiscal",
        caveat="Baisse uniforme d'environ 2,5 points du taux apparent : le modèle n'a "
               "qu'un seul taux d'imposition sur le revenu pour tous les salariés, donc "
               "il ne représente AUCUN effet de barème ni de progressivité."),
    "taxe_carbone": VariantSpec(
        "Hausse de la taxe carbone de 1 pt de PIB", -1, "ex_ante_fiscal",
        caveat="Le choc porte sur les VOLUMES d'énergie, et p121 avertit qu'il est "
               "difficile de transposer des points de PIB en euros par tonne de CO2 : "
               "« le calibrage d'une taxe carbone doit donc être réalisé hors modèle »."),
    "cotisations_employeurs_ciblees": VariantSpec(
        "Impact d’une baisse uniforme des cotisations sociales employeurs de 1 % du PIB "
        "ex ante, ciblée sur les salaires situés entre 1 et 1,6 Smic", +1,
        "ex_ante_fiscal", targeted=True, rows=ROWS_TARGETED,
        caveat="Encadré 14, présenté « à visée illustrative uniquement », et la note 79 "
               "précise que « son impact ne permet pas d'évaluer l'effet de mesures "
               "d'allègement de cotisations spécifiquement mises en place au cours des "
               "dernières années ». À utiliser malgré tout pour un allègement bas "
               "salaires : la variante uniforme donne 290 000 emplois à trois ans contre "

class MesangeError(RuntimeError):
    """The Mésange document cannot be read as expected."""


#: The cost the ENGINE prices for a variant's instrument, in points of the variant per

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Variant:
    """One published variant, in the expansionary convention."""

    key: str
    spec: VariantSpec
    rows: dict[str, tuple[float, ...]]
    page: int
    """1-based PDF page. The printed folio is this minus one — the public-investment
    table is folio 102 and PDF page 103 — so a citation must say which it means."""

    @property
    def shock(self) -> str:
        return self.spec.shock

    @property
    def published_sign(self) -> int:
        return self.spec.expansionary_sign

    @property
    def caveat(self) -> str:
        return self.spec.caveat

    def at(self, row: str, horizon: str) -> float:
        if row not in self.rows:
            raise MesangeError(f"variant {self.key!r} has no row {row!r}")
        if horizon not in HORIZONS:
            raise MesangeError(f"unknown horizon {horizon!r}; have {HORIZONS}")
        return self.rows[row][HORIZONS.index(horizon)]

    @property
    def multiplier(self) -> tuple[float, ...]:
        """GDP response per point of GDP of expansionary impulse, by horizon."""
        return self.rows["gdp"]

    @property
    def jobs(self) -> tuple[float, ...]:
        """Thousands of market-sector employees, by horizon."""
        return self.rows["emploi_milliers"]


def _normalise(text: str) -> str:
    """Collapse whitespace and settle the apostrophe.

    The document uses U+2019 throughout; extractors and editors do not always agree,
    and a shock sentence that fails to match by one apostrophe would raise as a missing
    variant rather than as the encoding problem it is.
    """
    return " ".join(text.replace("\u0027", "\u2019").split())


def _numbers(line: str, label: str) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    tail = line[len(label):]
    # French decimals, and a minus sign that the extractor renders as a hyphen.
    found = re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:[,.]\d+)?", tail)
    values = tuple(float(v.replace(",", ".")) for v in found)
    if len(values) != len(HORIZONS):
        raise MesangeError(
            f"row {label!r} yielded {len(values)} numbers, expected {len(HORIZONS)}: "
            f"{values}"
        )
    return values


def load(raw: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, Variant]:
    """Every budgetary variant, parsed from the published document.

    Raises on any variant it cannot find. A missing multiplier must kill its feature
    rather than fall back to a neighbour's number.
    """
    path = (raw or RAW) / SOURCE_FILE
    if not path.exists():
        raise MesangeError(f"{path} not found — download it and record it in the manifest "
                           f"(`impots data fetch {path.name}`)")
    if importlib.util.find_spec("pypdf") is None:  # pragma: no cover - environment
        raise MesangeError("pypdf is required to read the Mésange document")

    pages = _pages(str(path))

    variants: dict[str, Variant] = {}
    for key, spec in VARIANTS.items():
        target = _normalise(spec.shock)
        sign = spec.expansionary_sign
        labels = spec.rows or ROWS
        for number, lines in pages:
            # Matched against the joined page rather than line by line: the targeted
            # variant's title wraps mid-sentence in the extraction. The safeguard
            # against the anchor appearing elsewhere (the public-investment sentence is
            # also on p52 and p136) stays what it was — every expected row must be on
            # the same page, and only the first qualifying page is kept.
            if target not in " ".join(lines):
                continue
            rows = {}
            for name, label in labels.items():
                line = next((line for line in lines if line.startswith(label)), None)
                if line is None:
                    break
                # The whole table flips together, the primary balance included: the
                # convention reverses the SHOCK, not a selection of its consequences.
                # A VAT rise improving the balance by 0.80 becomes a VAT cut costing
                # 0.80, and the row keeps corresponding to the same simulated measure.
                # Legitimate only because the model is linear, which is why the
                # symmetry assumption is stated on every row that carries it.
                values = _numbers(line, label)
                rows[name] = values if sign > 0 else tuple(-v for v in values)
            if len(rows) != len(labels):
                continue
            variants[key] = Variant(key=key, spec=spec, rows=rows, page=number)
            break
        else:
            raise MesangeError(
                f"variant {key!r} not found: no page carries the shock sentence "
                f"{spec.shock!r} together with all of {sorted(labels)}. The document "
                f"may have been revised — do not guess a value."
            )
    return variants


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _pages(path: str) -> tuple[tuple[int, tuple[str, ...]], ...]:
    """Extracted lines per page, cached: 150 pages of PDF is seconds, and the tests
    read the same document a dozen times. Returns tuples so the cache cannot be
    mutated by a caller."""
    import pypdf

    return tuple(
        (i + 1, tuple(_normalise(line) for line in (page.extract_text() or "").splitlines()))
        for i, page in enumerate(pypdf.PdfReader(path).pages)
    )


def printed_row(variant: Variant, label: str, raw: Path | None = None
                ) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """Another row of a variant's own table, by the label its left column prints, in
    the expansionary convention (the whole table flips together, as in `load`). Read
    from the page `load` kept for the variant; a label absent from that page, or printed
    twice, is refused. Used by the twin's coherence table (D-418) for the unemployment
    rate and the consumer price rows, which `ROWS` does not carry."""
    path = (raw or RAW) / SOURCE_FILE
    if not path.exists():
        raise MesangeError(f"{path} not found — `impots data fetch {path.name}`")
    lines = dict(_pages(str(path)))[variant.page]
    target = _normalise(label)
    found = [line for line in lines if line.startswith(target)
             and re.match(r"\s*-?\d", line[len(target):])]
    if len(found) != 1:
        raise MesangeError(f"variant {variant.key!r}, p. {variant.page}: {len(found)} rows "
                           f"{label!r}")
    values = _numbers(found[0], target)
    return values if variant.published_sign > 0 else tuple(-v for v in values)


def table(row: str, raw: Path | None = None, absent_for: tuple[str, ...] | list[str] = (),
          ) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[float, ...]], tuple[str, ...]]:
    """One row of every variant, as (values by instrument, horizons).

    The adapter the parameter store addresses every reader through, so that adding a
    source does not mean adding a branch to the store.

    `absent_for` names the variants the YAML DECLARES do not print this row — the
    targeted variant has no balance row (D-214). Declared, not tolerated: a variant
    missing the row without being named is still refused, and a variant named that does
    print it is refused too, because the declaration would then be stale and the row
    silently narrower than the document.
    """
    variants = load(raw=raw)
    declared = set(absent_for)
    unknown = sorted(declared - set(variants))
    if unknown:
        raise MesangeError(f"absent_for names variants that do not exist: {unknown}")
    stale = sorted(k for k in declared if row in variants[k].rows)
    if stale:
        raise MesangeError(f"row {row!r} is declared absent for {stale}, which print it")
    missing = [key for key, variant in variants.items()
               if row not in variant.rows and key not in declared]
    if missing:
        raise MesangeError(f"row {row!r} absent from variants {missing}")
    return {key: variant.rows[row] for key, variant in variants.items()
            if key not in declared}, HORIZONS


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the wage-formation sensitivity (§4.4, folios 137 and 138), the « variante salariale »
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#: The two tables §4.4 prints for the wage formation, by title, and the variants each
#: carries under the alternative (D-349). Under a Phillips curve (folio 137) the document
#: runs the employer contributions and VAT only; for the employee contributions, the CSG
#: and the income tax, the alternative it prints is the super-gross wage targeted in the
#: long run (folio 138), the other half of the same question: whether a cut in the tax
#: wedge lowers equilibrium unemployment for good.
SENSIBILITE_TABLES = {
    "phillips": ("Sensibilité des variantes à la forme de la négociation salariale",
                 ("cotisations_employeurs", "tva")),
    "super_brut": ("Sensibilité des variantes fiscales à l’élasticité des salaires au coin "
                   "fiscalo social",
                   ("cotisations_salaries", "csg", "impot_sur_le_revenu")),
}
#: The block labels as the extraction joins them, to the variant they name.
SENSIBILITE_LABELS = {
    "Cotisations sociales employeurs": "cotisations_employeurs",
    "Cotisations sociales employeur": "cotisations_employeurs",
    "TVA": "tva",
    "Cotisations sociales salariés": "cotisations_salaries",
    "Contribution sociale généralisée": "csg",
    "Impôt sur le revenu": "impot_sur_le_revenu",
}
SENSIBILITE_HORIZONS = ("1", "5", "10")


def sensibilite_salariale(raw: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """By instrument: the GDP row at 1, 5 and 10 years under the central model and under
    the alternative wage formation, and which table it comes from (D-349).

    Each table prints, per variant, a « PIB » line of eight numbers: 1A 5A 10A LT for the
    central model, then the same for the alternative. The central half is checked
    against the variant's own table; a block the reader cannot find, or a central column
    that is not the variant's, is refused by name."""
    path = (raw or RAW) / SOURCE_FILE
    if not path.exists():
        raise MesangeError(f"{path} not found — `impots data fetch {path.name}`")
    pages = _pages(str(path))
    variants = load(raw=raw)
    out: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for table_key, (title, wanted) in SENSIBILITE_TABLES.items():
        target = _normalise(title)
        page = next(((n, lines) for n, lines in pages if target in " ".join(lines)), None)
        if page is None:
            raise MesangeError(f"tableau « {title} » introuvable")
        number, lines = page
        label: list[str] = []
        found: dict[str, tuple[float, ...]] = {}
        for line in lines:
            if line.startswith("PIB "):
                name = SENSIBILITE_LABELS.get(" ".join(label).strip())
                values = tuple(float(v.replace(",", "."))
                               for v in re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:,\d+)?", line[4:]))
                if name is not None and len(values) == 8:
                    found[name] = values
                label = []
            elif line.startswith(("Emploi", "IPC", "%", "Modèle", "Négociation", "1A",
                                  "setting", "Salaire", "β")) or re.match(r"^\d", line):
                label = []
            else:
                label.append(line)
        for name in wanted:
            if name not in found:
                raise MesangeError(f"« {title} » (p. {number}) : pas de ligne PIB pour "
                                   f"{name}")
            values = found[name]
            sign = VARIANTS[name].expansionary_sign
            central = {h: sign * values[i] for i, h in enumerate(SENSIBILITE_HORIZONS)}
            alternative = {h: sign * values[4 + i]
                           for i, h in enumerate(SENSIBILITE_HORIZONS)}
            pib = variants[name].rows["gdp"]
            own = {h: pib[HORIZONS.index(h)] for h in SENSIBILITE_HORIZONS}
            if any(abs(central[h] - own[h]) > 1e-9 for h in SENSIBILITE_HORIZONS):
                raise MesangeError(f"{name} : la colonne centrale de « {title} » {central} "
                                   f"n'est pas la variante {own} — lecture décalée")
            out[name] = {"table": table_key, "page": number, "central": central,
                         "alternative": alternative}
    return out

"""B1 — shock construction (PHASE4_SPEC §1).

Turns what the lower layers measured into a dated net fiscal impulse, labelled by
instrument, with the product allocation B2 needs to give it a shape.

**No propensity to consume appears here, and that is not an omission.** §1's sketch
routes household income deltas through an MPC to get a consumption impulse. That step
would double-count: Mésange's income-tax multiplier is the GDP response to an
income-tax cut, and the household decision to spend rather than save is already inside
it. B1 therefore stops at the fiscal impulse per instrument and lets the multiplier do
the rest — which is also why `mpc_by_income_position` dying (D-052) costs less than it
appeared to. It cost the decile differentiation, not the channel.

**The double-entry rule extends here** (D-045): the instrument impulses must add back to
the reform's own net cost. A shock that does not balance is not a smaller shock, it is a
mis-specified one, and `assert_balanced` refuses it.

**Instruments without a multiplier are refused, not approximated.** The mapping below is
deliberately partial, and the gaps are the interesting part.
"""

#: Knobs whose reforms are CONCENTRATED ON LOW WAGES, and which must therefore route
#: employer contributions to the targeted variant rather than the uniform one.

class ShockError(RuntimeError):
    """A shock cannot be constructed from what the lower layers reported."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Impulse:
    """A dated net fiscal impulse, labelled by instrument."""

    year: int
    by_instrument: dict[str, float]
    """Euros, expansionary-positive, keyed by Mésange variant."""
    unmapped: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    """Deltas with no multiplier. Not dropped — carried, so the caller must decide
    whether to report a partial macro path or refuse one."""
    net_fiscal_eur: float = 0.0

    @property
    def total(self) -> float:
        return sum(self.by_instrument.values())

    @property
    def unmapped_total(self) -> float:
        return sum(self.unmapped.values())

    @property
    def covered_share(self) -> float:
        """Share of the reform's movement that has a multiplier at all.

        GROSS magnitudes on both sides, never the signed totals: a benefit rise and a
        corporate tax cut are two uncovered instruments, and letting them cancel in the
        denominator would report a reform as better covered the more of it is missing.
        """
        mapped = sum(abs(v) for v in self.by_instrument.values())
        missing = sum(abs(v) for v in self.unmapped.values())
        moved = mapped + missing
        return mapped / moved if moved > 0 else 0.0

    def reasons(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        return {
            name: UNMAPPED_REASONS[UNMAPPED[name]]
            for name in self.unmapped
            if name in UNMAPPED
        }


def targets_low_wages(knobs: tuple[str, ...] | None, year: int | None = None) -> bool:
    """Whether this reform's knobs concentrate on low wages, in `year`.

    Decided from the KNOBS the reform moved, not from its deltas: the population layer
    reports one employer-contribution total either way, so the delta cannot tell a
    uniform rate cut from an allègement. From `REFONTE_YEAR`, the ceiling is no longer
    one of them (D-239).
    """
    return any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(knob, pattern)
        for knob in (knobs or ())
        if not (year is not None and year >= REFONTE_YEAR
                and knob in EXIT_THRESHOLD_KNOBS)
        for pattern in TARGETED_EMPLOYER_KNOBS
    )


def instrument_deltas(deltas: dict[str, float], *,
                      employer_contribution_delta: float = 0.0) -> dict[str, float]:
    """The deltas `build` reads, out of everything the population layer reports.

    `aggregate.deltas` carries every total the runner reports: salaries, disposable
    income, and the components of the income tax (`ir_avant_niches`, `reductions`,
    `credits_impot`) beside `ir` itself. Handed to `build` whole, the first of those
    raised — which is how every reform's macro path came back unavailable on the real
    population (D-218). Counted, the components would double the shock. So this keeps
    exactly the instruments `guards.sector_balance` counts, in its convention:

    * the state's receipts (`guards.STATE_RECEIPTS`), receipts-positive as reported;
    * the transfers it pays (`guards.STATE_TRANSFERS`), whose positive delta means the
      state pays MORE — negated here into the receipts-positive convention `build` reads;
    * the employer contributions actually paid, net of allègements, under the name
      `INSTRUMENT_MAP` gives them. `cotisations_employeur` is gross of the allègements
      and does not move when one changes (`aggregate._employer_contribution_delta`).
    """
    from impots.guards import STATE_RECEIPTS, STATE_TRANSFERS

    out = {name: deltas[name] for name in STATE_RECEIPTS if deltas.get(name)}
    out.update({name: -deltas[name] for name in STATE_TRANSFERS if deltas.get(name)})
    if employer_contribution_delta:
        out["employer_contributions"] = employer_contribution_delta
    return out


def build(deltas: dict[str, float], *, year: int,
          reform_cost: float | None = None,
          knobs: tuple[str, ...] | None = None) -> Impulse:
    """Map lower-layer deltas onto instrument impulses.

    `deltas` are receipts-positive as the population layer reports them — a tax rise is
    a positive delta — so each is negated into the expansionary convention. `knobs` are
    the reform's own knob names, needed only to tell a targeted employer-contribution
    reform from a uniform one, which the deltas cannot.
    """
    targeted = targets_low_wages(knobs, year)
    by_instrument: dict[str, float] = {}
    unmapped: dict[str, float] = {}
    for name, value in deltas.items():
        if value == 0.0:
            continue
        if name in INSTRUMENT_MAP:
            variant = INSTRUMENT_MAP[name]
            if variant == "cotisations_employeurs" and targeted:
                variant = "cotisations_employeurs_ciblees"
            by_instrument[variant] = by_instrument.get(variant, 0.0) - value
        elif name in UNMAPPED:
            unmapped[name] = -value
        else:
            raise ShockError(
                f"delta {name!r} is neither mapped to a multiplier nor listed as "
                f"unmapped. Add it to one or the other: silently ignoring it would "
                f"make the shock smaller than the reform without saying so."
            )
    unknown = set(by_instrument) - set(mesange.VARIANTS)
    if unknown:
        raise ShockError(f"instruments with no published variant: {sorted(unknown)}")
    return Impulse(year=year, by_instrument=by_instrument, unmapped=unmapped,
                   net_fiscal_eur=reform_cost if reform_cost is not None else 0.0)


def assert_balanced(impulse: Impulse, reform_cost: float, *,
                    rtol: float = BALANCE_RTOL) -> None:
    """Double entry (D-045): the impulse must add back to the reform's own cost.

    Compared on MAGNITUDE, not on a signed residual: for a cost, a larger miss reads as
    a smaller number, so a one-sided bound on the signed value passes exactly the cases
    it should fail. That mistake has been made once in this repository already.
    """
    constructed = impulse.total + impulse.unmapped_total
    expected = -reform_cost
    scale = max(abs(expected), MINIMUM_IMPULSE_EUR)
    residual = abs(constructed - expected)
    if residual / scale > rtol:
        raise ShockError(
            f"the constructed impulse ({constructed:,.0f} EUR) does not reconstitute "
            f"the reform's net cost ({expected:,.0f} EUR): off by {residual:,.0f}, "
            f"{residual / scale:.2%} of scale. An unbalanced shock is mis-specified, "
            f"not small."
        )


def allocation(tes: Tes, impulse: Impulse) -> np.ndarray:
    """Total final demand by product for this impulse, for B2 to compose.

    Each instrument is allocated on the published final-use column its money actually
    moves through, then the instruments are summed. An impulse whose instruments pull in
    opposite directions is refused rather than netted: netting would allocate the
    residual on a mix belonging to neither, and B2 cannot compose a negative demand.
    """
    if not impulse.by_instrument:
        raise ShockError("no mapped instrument: this reform has no macro path")
    signs = {np.sign(v) for v in impulse.by_instrument.values() if v != 0}
    if len(signs) > 1:
        raise ShockError(
            "instruments pull in opposite directions; compose each side separately, "
            "since a netted allocation would use a product mix belonging to neither"
        )
    total = np.zeros(tes.n)
    for variant, value in impulse.by_instrument.items():
        basis = ALLOCATION_BASIS.get(variant)
        if basis is None:
            raise ShockError(f"no allocation basis declared for {variant!r}")
        vector = (tes.final_uses[basis] + tes.imported_final_uses[basis]).clip(min=0.0)
        if vector.sum() <= 0:
            raise ShockError(f"allocation basis {basis!r} is empty")
        total += vector / vector.sum() * abs(value)
    return total

"""The macro parameter store (PHASE4_SPEC §2).

The behavioural store's rule, extended one step: a row loads only with a verifier's
verdict, and a row that dies is **removed with its reason** rather than softened. What
is new here is where the numbers come from.

**Table-valued rows carry no numbers in YAML.** A multiplier is not one figure but
eight instruments times six horizons, and retyping forty-eight numbers into a
configuration file is precisely the transcription D-026 forbids. So `multipliers.yaml`
declares `from_source_table: gdp` and the values are parsed out of the published PDF by
`impots.macro.mesange`. The YAML holds what the PDF cannot: scope, support, the
verdict, and the reasons a row is narrower than someone might wish.

That inverts the usual failure. A stale YAML cannot drift away from its source, because
there is nothing in it to drift; but a source file that goes missing kills its rows
loudly, which is the direction this project wants to fail in.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import yaml

from impots.behavioural.store import (
    LOADABLE_VERDICTS,
    Confidence,
    Distribution,
    Parameter,
    Source,
    Support,
    UnverifiedParameter,
    Verifier,
)
from impots.macro import imk, mesange

PARAMETERS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "parameters"

#: Readers a `source_table` block may name. A YAML file cannot nominate arbitrary
#: import paths: the point of parsing from the primary file is that the parser is
#: reviewed code, and an open-ended importer would hand that property back.
READERS = {"impots.macro.mesange": mesange, "impots.macro.imk": imk}


#: Reform knobs that move transfers (PHASE9_SPEC §5, D-219). A macro row claiming one of
#: them is a transfers multiplier, and the only sources for one are two international
#: meta-analyses that disagree on the centre and by a factor 2,5 on the width, with no
#: horizon profile and no balance row (M0, R4). Such a row may load only as
#: `confidence: low` and graded illustrative from the first euro.
TRANSFER_KNOBS = ("af_*", "al_*", "ppa_*", "rsa_*")


class MissingSourceTable(RuntimeError):
    """A table-valued parameter's primary file is absent."""


class UngradedTransferRow(UnverifiedParameter):
    """A row claiming transfer knobs tried to load above `confidence: low`, or graded in
    support: the evidence for a transfers multiplier does not carry either."""


def _claims_transfers(body: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Whether any knob pattern the row declares overlaps a transfer knob, read both
    ways so that `*` and `rsa_montant_de_base` are caught as surely as `rsa_*`."""
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(declared, pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(pattern, declared)
               for declared in (body.get("responds_to_knobs") or ())
               for pattern in TRANSFER_KNOBS)


def _transfer_problem(body: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    if not _claims_transfers(body):
        return ""
    support = (body.get("support") or {}).get("max_variation_graded_in_support")
    if body.get("confidence") != "low" or support != 0:
        return (f"la ligne revendique des leviers de transferts (confiance "
                f"{body.get('confidence', 'medium')!r}, support {support!r}) : elle ne "
                f"charge qu'en `confidence: low`, avec un support nul qui la note "
                f"illustrative dès le premier euro (§5, D-219)")
    return ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TableParameter:
    """A parameter whose value is a table read from a primary document.

    `values[instrument][horizon]` — no central/low/high, because the source publishes
    a profile per instrument and flattening it to one figure is how the spec's seeds
    came to be a year-one range wearing no horizon.
    """

    key: str
    values: dict[str, tuple[float, ...]]
    horizons: tuple[str, ...]
    """Every horizon the source publishes."""
    usable_horizons: tuple[str, ...]
    """The subset this project will read. Narrower than `horizons` for the Mésange
    rows, and for two independent reasons that agree: §0 refuses any horizon past three
    years, and the sensitivity analysis shows the long columns are determined by a
    specification choice rather than measured — employer contributions run 1.73 at LT
    under wage-setting and 0.25 under a Phillips curve. Reading a column the source
    publishes but the project will not stand behind is how an unusable figure reaches a
    reader."""
    applies_to: str
    support: Support
    source: Source
    verifier: Verifier
    confidence: Confidence = "medium"
    distribution: Distribution = "triangular"
    responds_to_knobs: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    note: str = ""

    def at(self, instrument: str, horizon: str) -> float:
        if instrument not in self.values:
            raise KeyError(
                f"{self.key}: no instrument {instrument!r}. Instruments without a "
                f"published variant have no multiplier and must not borrow one; "
                f"have {sorted(self.values)}"
            )
        if horizon not in self.usable_horizons:
            published = " (published but not usable here)" if horizon in self.horizons else ""
            raise KeyError(
                f"{self.key}: horizon {horizon!r}{published}; usable horizons are "
                f"{self.usable_horizons}"
            )
        return self.values[instrument][self.horizons.index(horizon)]

    def profile(self, instrument: str) -> tuple[float, ...]:
        """The usable horizons only, in order — never the published tail."""
        if instrument not in self.values:
            raise KeyError(f"{self.key}: no instrument {instrument!r}")
        return tuple(self.at(instrument, h) for h in self.usable_horizons)


@dataclass
class Store:
    parameters: dict[str, Parameter] = field(default_factory=dict)
    tables: dict[str, TableParameter] = field(default_factory=dict)
    thresholds: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    rejected: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    removed: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    """Rows deliberately killed, with the reason. A feature resting on one reports
    'no usable evidence, because ...' rather than quietly having fewer inputs."""

    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> Parameter:
        return self.parameters[key]

    def __contains__(self, key: str) -> bool:
        return key in self.parameters or key in self.tables

    def why_removed(self, key: str) -> str:
        """The reason a feature is dead, for the assumptions strip to print."""
        if key in self.removed:
            return self.removed[key]
        if key in self.rejected:
            return self.rejected[key]
        raise KeyError(f"{key!r} was not removed or rejected")

    def vintage(self) -> str:
        keys = ",".join(sorted([*self.parameters, *self.tables]))
        return f"{len(self.parameters) + len(self.tables)} rows [{keys}]"


def _support(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Support:
    bound = raw.get("max_variation_graded_in_support")
    return Support(
        estimated_on=raw.get("estimated_on", ""),
        max_variation_graded_in_support=None if bound is None else float(bound),
    )


def _source(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Source:
    return Source(citation=raw.get("citation", ""), url=raw.get("url", ""),
                  vintage=str(raw.get("vintage", "")), quote=raw.get("quote", ""))


def _verifier(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Verifier:
    return Verifier(verdict=raw.get("verdict"), date=str(raw.get("date") or ""),
                    ref=raw.get("ref") or "", note=raw.get("note", ""))


def _scalar(key: str, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Parameter:
    value = raw["value"]
    return Parameter(
        key=key, central=float(value["central"]), low=float(value["low"]),
        high=float(value["high"]), distribution=value.get("distribution", "triangular"),
        applies_to=raw.get("applies_to", ""),
        responds_to_knobs=tuple(raw.get("responds_to_knobs") or ()),
        support=_support(raw.get("support") or {}), source=_source(raw.get("source") or {}),
        verifier=_verifier(raw.get("verifier") or {}),
        confidence=raw.get("confidence", "medium"), note=raw.get("note", ""),
    )


def _table(key: str, raw: dict[str, Any], declared: dict[str, Any],
           raw_dir: Path | None) -> TableParameter:
    reader_name = declared.get("reader")
    reader = READERS.get(reader_name)
    if reader is None:
        raise MissingSourceTable(
            f"{key}: source_table names reader {reader_name!r}, which is not one of "
            f"{sorted(READERS)}. Readers are reviewed code, not a YAML import path."
        )
    value = raw["value"]
    # Everything in the value block other than the row name and the distribution is an
    # argument for the reader, so a second document is a data change, not a code change.
    options = {k: v for k, v in value.items()
               if k not in ("from_source_table", "distribution")}
    declared_usable = options.pop("usable_horizons", None)
    values, horizons = reader.table(value["from_source_table"], raw=raw_dir, **options)
    usable = tuple(declared_usable) if declared_usable else horizons
    unknown = set(usable) - set(horizons)
    if unknown:
        raise MissingSourceTable(
            f"{key}: usable_horizons names {sorted(unknown)}, which the source does "
            f"not publish; it has {horizons}"
        )
    return TableParameter(
        key=key,
        values=values,
        horizons=horizons,
        usable_horizons=usable,
        applies_to=raw.get("applies_to", ""),
        responds_to_knobs=tuple(raw.get("responds_to_knobs") or ()),
        support=_support(raw.get("support") or {}), source=_source(declared),
        verifier=_verifier(raw.get("verifier") or {}),
        confidence=raw.get("confidence", "medium"),
        distribution=value.get("distribution", "triangular"),
        note=raw.get("note", ""),
    )


def load(directory: Path | None = None, *, strict: bool = True,
         raw: Path | None = None) -> Store:
    """Load the macro store, refusing anything a verifier has not passed.

    `strict=False` records refusals in `Store.rejected` rather than raising. It exists
    for the report that lists what is missing and why — never for a band. Producing a
    number is always strict.
    """
    store = Store()
    for path in sorted((directory or PARAMETERS).glob("*.yaml")):
        document = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
        store.thresholds.update(document.get("thresholds") or {})
        store.removed.update(document.get("removed") or {})
        declared = document.get("source_table") or {}
        for key, body in (document.get("parameters") or {}).items():
            verdict = (body.get("verifier") or {}).get("verdict")
            if verdict not in LOADABLE_VERDICTS:
                reason = (
                    f"verdict {verdict!r} — only {sorted(LOADABLE_VERDICTS)} load. "
                    f"{(body.get('verifier') or {}).get('note', '').strip()}"
                )
                if strict:
                    raise UnverifiedParameter(f"{path.name}:{key}: {reason}")
                store.rejected[key] = reason
                continue
            problem = _transfer_problem(body)
            if problem:
                if strict:
                    raise UngradedTransferRow(f"{path.name}:{key}: {problem}")
                store.rejected[key] = problem
                continue
            if "from_source_table" in (body.get("value") or {}):
                store.tables[key] = _table(key, body, declared, raw)
            else:
                store.parameters[key] = _scalar(key, body)
    return store


def draw(parameter: Parameter, rng: np.random.Generator, size: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample a scalar parameter. Delegates, so both stores share one sampler."""
    return parameter.draw(rng, size)

"""Reading INSEE's symmetric input-output table (M0).

Reading, not propagating. `scripts/verify_tes.py` must be green and `docs/M0_TES.md`
written before any Leontief code exists — the EEC's M0 changed the shape of its
problem, and this gate is why that is now a procedure rather than a memory.

The file is the *TES symétrique* — branch × branch, already converted from the
supply-use form, which is the object a Leontief inverse needs. It ships as three
sheets: a presentation note, the domestic table, and a separate import matrix. The
second is what the composition comes from; the third is what measures leakage, which
§1 requires to be computed rather than assumed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

RAW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "data" / "raw"

DOMESTIC_SHEET = "TES de production domestique"
IMPORTS_SHEET = "TES des importations"

#: Where each block begins and ends is DISCOVERED per sheet, not assumed.
#:
#: The two sheets do not share a layout, and assuming they did is the first thing M0
#: caught: on the domestic sheet the intermediate matrix starts at column 45 and the
#: product codes sit in column 3, while on the import sheet the matrix starts at
#: column 10 and the codes sit in column 9. A reader carrying one set of constants
#: reads the import matrix out of the wrong columns and raises — or worse, does not.
#:
#: The block is found by its own headers: row 6 announces it, row 8 closes it.
BLOCK_START_MARKER = "ENTREES INTERM"
BLOCK_END_MARKER = "Total des entrées interm"
CODE_ROW = 9
FIRST_PRODUCT_ROW = 11
HEADER_ROW = 8
BLOCK_TITLE_ROW = 6

#: Final-use columns, matched by the header text the sheet prints above them, as
#: (header, exact-match, sub-code).
#:
#: The third element is the finding that made this table's M0 worth running. Final
#: consumption is published as FOUR columns under ONE merged header — Ménages, APU,
#: ISBLSM, TOTAL — with the institutional sector written on the code row beneath.
#: Matching the header alone returns its leftmost column, so `consommation_finale`
#: silently meant *households only*: 1 158.7 bn where the total is 1 888.2 bn. The
#: balance identity did not catch it, because that identity is built on "Total des
#: emplois finals", a separate column that is correct either way. It surfaced only
#: from adding the components up by hand and finding 730 bn missing.
#:
#: The institutional split is kept rather than discarded: a public-spending shock and
#: a household-transfer shock enter the macro layer through different columns, and the
#: MPC that applies to one does not apply to the other.
FINAL_USE_MARKERS: dict[str, tuple[str, bool, str | None]] = {
    "consommation_finale_menages": ("Dépenses de consommation finale (1)", True, "Ménages"),
    "consommation_finale_apu": ("Dépenses de consommation finale (1)", True, "APU"),
    "consommation_finale_isblsm": ("Dépenses de consommation finale (1)", True, "ISBLSM"),
    "consommation_finale": ("Dépenses de consommation finale (1)", True, "TOTAL"),
    "fbcf": ("Formation brute de capital fixe (1)", True, None),
    "objets_de_valeur": ("Acq. moins cessions d'objets de valeur (1)", True, None),
    "variation_stocks": ("Variation de stocks (1)", True, None),
    "formation_brute_capital": ("Formation brute de capital (1)", True, None),
    "exportations": ("Exportations", True, None),
    "total_emplois_finals": ("Total des emplois finals", True, None),
    "total_emplois": ("Total des emplois", True, None),
}


#: The import sheet prints the same final-use blocks under two different total labels,
#: so the two totals need an override there. Everything else matches by the same header.
#:
#: Reading them matters more than it looks: final demand for a product is met partly by
#: domestic production and partly by imports, and only the first sets off a Leontief
#: round. Without this block the direct import channel is invisible and the leakage
#: correction reports roughly half of what it should.
IMPORT_FINAL_USE_OVERRIDES = {
    "total_emplois_finals": "Total des emplois finals en importations",
    "total_emplois": "Total des emplois en importations",
}


#: Rows below the 37 products that carry the reconciliation to acquisition prices.
#: Found by reading the sheet, not assumed: the symmetric table is published at BASIC
#: prices, so its totals are about 200 bn short of GDP until taxes less subsidies on
#: products and the two corrections are added back.
RECONCILIATION_ROWS = {
    "domestique": "TOTAL",
    "importations_caf": "UTILISATION DE PRODUITS IMPORT",
    "taxes_moins_subventions": "TAXES MOINS SUBVENTIONS SUR LES PRODUITS",
    "correction_territoriale": "CORRECTION TERRITORIALE",
    "correction_caf_fab": "CORRECTION CAF FAB",
    "prix_acquisition": "TOTAL AU PRIX D",
}


class TesError(RuntimeError):
    """The input-output table cannot be read as expected."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tes:
    """One vintage of the symmetric table, in millions of euros."""

    branches: tuple[str, ...]
    labels: tuple[str, ...]
    domestic: np.ndarray
    """Intermediate consumption, domestic production. `domestic[i, j]` is product i
    consumed by branch j."""
    imported: np.ndarray
    """The same, for imported product. Its row sums are the leakage §1 needs."""
    final_uses: dict[str, np.ndarray]
    """Final uses met by DOMESTIC production, by product."""
    imported_final_uses: dict[str, np.ndarray]
    """The same final uses met by IMPORTS. Together with `final_uses` these give the
    domestic/import split of each category of final demand — the direct leakage channel,
    which is invisible if only the domestic sheet is read."""
    total_output: np.ndarray
    """Total resources of each product at basic prices, domestic production only."""
    vintage: str
    source_file: str

    @property
    def n(self) -> int:
        return len(self.branches)

    @property
    def base_year(self) -> int:
        """The year the table describes, taken from the vintage rather than the clock.

        Pairing a 2022 table with 2023 employment would silently misstate every
        employment coefficient, so the year travels with the table.
        """
        return int(self.vintage[:4])


def _sheet(path: Path, name: str) -> Any:
    try:
        import openpyxl
    except ModuleNotFoundError as error:  # pragma: no cover - environment
        raise TesError("openpyxl is required to read the TES") from error
    if not path.exists():
        raise TesError(f"{path} not found — download it and record it in the manifest")
    workbook = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    if name not in workbook.sheetnames:
        raise TesError(f"{path.name} has no sheet {name!r}; got {workbook.sheetnames}")
    return workbook[name]


def _number(value: Any) -> float:
    if value is None or value == "":
        return 0.0
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        raise TesError(f"expected a number, got {value!r}") from error


def _find(sheet: Any, row: int, marker: str, *, exact: bool = False) -> int | None:
    """Leftmost column on `row` whose header matches `marker`.

    `exact` exists because two of the headers are prefixes of each other: "Total des
    emplois" is contained in "Total des emplois finals", which sits to its left, so a
    substring search returns the same column for both and the two totals come back
    identical — 3 245.8 bn each, where the real values differ by the whole
    intermediate block. Found by reading the numbers rather than by the code failing.
    """
    for column in range(1, sheet.max_column + 1):
        value = sheet.cell(row, column).value
        if not value:
            continue
        text = " ".join(str(value).split())
        if (text.lower() == marker.lower()) if exact else (marker.lower() in text.lower()):
            return column
    return None


def _subcolumn(sheet: Any, header_column: int, subcode: str, key: str) -> int:
    """The column under a merged header carrying `subcode` on the code row.

    Walks right from the header until the next header begins. Raises rather than
    falling back to the header column: a silent fallback is exactly how
    `consommation_finale` came to mean households only.
    """
    column = header_column
    while column <= sheet.max_column:
        if column > header_column and sheet.cell(HEADER_ROW, column).value:
            break
        found = " ".join(str(sheet.cell(CODE_ROW, column).value or "").split())
        if found.lower() == subcode.lower():
            return column
        column += 1
    raise TesError(
        f"final-use column {key!r}: no sub-column {subcode!r} under its header at "
        f"column {header_column}"
    )


def gdp(table: Tes, raw: Path | None = None) -> float:
    """GDP at market prices, in millions of euros, from the table's own identity.

    Needed because the employment coefficients are published per POINT OF GDP, so
    converting them to a job count requires the GDP the point is a point of. The
    multiplier itself does not: a GDP response per point of GDP of impulse, applied to
    an impulse in euros, gives euros with the level cancelling.

    GDP = total final uses at acquisition prices − total imports. Reading the domestic
    sheet alone gives a figure about 210 bn short, because the symmetric table is
    published at BASIC prices; the reconciliation rows below the products carry taxes
    less subsidies on products and the territorial and CAF/FAB corrections.
    """
    sheet = _sheet((raw or RAW) / f"insee_TES_symetrique_A38_{table.vintage}.xlsx",
                   DOMESTIC_SHEET)
    finals = _find(sheet, HEADER_ROW, "Total des emplois finals", exact=True)
    uses = _find(sheet, HEADER_ROW, "Total des emplois", exact=True)
    if finals is None or uses is None:
        raise TesError("cannot locate the final-use totals for the GDP identity")
    rows = _reconciliation_rows(sheet)
    acquisition = _number(sheet.cell(rows["prix_acquisition"], finals).value)
    imports = _number(sheet.cell(rows["importations_caf"], uses).value)
    return acquisition - imports


def _reconciliation_rows(sheet: Any) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Locate the reconciliation rows by their printed labels, not by offset."""
    found: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in range(FIRST_PRODUCT_ROW, sheet.max_row + 1):
        label = " ".join(str(sheet.cell(row, 2).value or "").split()).upper()
        if not label:
            continue
        for key, marker in RECONCILIATION_ROWS.items():
            if key not in found and label.startswith(marker.upper()):
                found[key] = row
    missing = set(RECONCILIATION_ROWS) - set(found)
    if missing:
        raise TesError(
            f"reconciliation rows {sorted(missing)} not found; the sheet layout may "
            f"have changed and GDP must not be guessed from an offset"
        )
    return found


def _final_uses(sheet: Any, product_rows: list[tuple[int, str]],
                overrides: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Every final-use column of one sheet, matched by its own headers."""
    uses: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    for key, (marker, exact, subcode) in FINAL_USE_MARKERS.items():
        column = _find(sheet, HEADER_ROW, overrides.get(key, marker), exact=exact)
        if column is None:
            raise TesError(
                f"final-use column {key!r} not found from its header on sheet "
                f"{sheet.title!r}"
            )
        if subcode is not None:
            column = _subcolumn(sheet, column, subcode, key)
        uses[key] = np.array([_number(sheet.cell(r, column).value) for r, _ in product_rows])
    return uses


def _geometry(sheet: Any) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, str]], list[tuple[int, str]]]:
    """(product rows, branch columns) for one sheet, from that sheet's own headers.

    The published symmetric table carries **37** branches, not the 38 its name
    suggests — an M0 finding, recorded rather than worked around. The rows also end
    with several literally labelled TOTAL, and the columns continue past the matrix
    into consumption by sector (Ménages, APU, ISBLSM); both are excluded by taking
    only what lies inside the announced block.
    """
    start = _find(sheet, BLOCK_TITLE_ROW, BLOCK_START_MARKER)
    end = _find(sheet, HEADER_ROW, BLOCK_END_MARKER)
    if start is None or end is None or end <= start:
        raise TesError(
            "could not locate the intermediate-consumption block from its own headers; "
            "the sheet layout has moved and the reader must be re-derived, not patched"
        )
    columns = [
        (c, str(sheet.cell(CODE_ROW, c).value).strip())
        for c in range(start, end)
        if sheet.cell(CODE_ROW, c).value
    ]
    branch_codes = {code for _, code in columns}
    # The product-code column is the one immediately left of the block that carries
    # the same codes going down.
    code_column = None
    for candidate in range(start - 1, 0, -1):
        found = [
            str(sheet.cell(r, candidate).value).strip()
            for r in range(FIRST_PRODUCT_ROW, sheet.max_row + 1)
            if sheet.cell(r, candidate).value
        ]
        if found and set(found) & branch_codes:
            code_column = candidate
            break
    if code_column is None:
        raise TesError("could not locate the product-code column beside the block")

    product_rows = [
        (r, str(sheet.cell(r, code_column).value).strip())
        for r in range(FIRST_PRODUCT_ROW, sheet.max_row + 1)
        if sheet.cell(r, code_column).value
        and str(sheet.cell(r, code_column).value).strip() in branch_codes
    ]
    if [code for _, code in product_rows] != [code for _, code in columns]:
        raise TesError(
            "the symmetric table's rows and columns are not the same branches in the "
            "same order, which every identity below assumes"
        )
    return product_rows, columns


def load(vintage: str = "2023SD", raw: Path | None = None) -> Tes:
    """Read one vintage. Millions of euros throughout, as published."""
    name = f"insee_TES_symetrique_A38_{vintage}.xlsx"
    path = (raw or RAW) / name
    domestic_sheet = _sheet(path, DOMESTIC_SHEET)
    import_sheet = _sheet(path, IMPORTS_SHEET)

    product_rows, branch_columns = _geometry(domestic_sheet)
    branches = tuple(code for _, code in product_rows)
    labels = tuple(
        str(domestic_sheet.cell(r, 2).value or "").strip() for r, _ in product_rows
    )
    n = len(branches)

    domestic = np.array([
        [_number(domestic_sheet.cell(r, c).value) for c, _ in branch_columns]
        for r, _ in product_rows
    ])

    # The import sheet repeats the layout on its own grid, so its coordinates are
    # resolved from its own headers rather than borrowed from the domestic one.
    import_rows, import_columns = _geometry(import_sheet)
    if [code for _, code in import_rows] != list(branches):
        raise TesError("the import matrix does not carry the same branches")
    imported = np.array([
        [_number(import_sheet.cell(r, c).value) for c, _ in import_columns]
        for r, _ in import_rows
    ])

    final_uses = _final_uses(domestic_sheet, product_rows, {})
    imported_final_uses = _final_uses(
        import_sheet, import_rows, IMPORT_FINAL_USE_OVERRIDES
    )
    total_output = final_uses["total_emplois"]

    if domestic.shape != (n, n) or imported.shape != (n, n):
        raise TesError(
            f"expected square {n}x{n} matrices, got {domestic.shape} and {imported.shape}"
        )
    return Tes(
        branches=branches, labels=labels, domestic=domestic, imported=imported,
        final_uses=final_uses, imported_final_uses=imported_final_uses,
        total_output=total_output, vintage=vintage, source_file=name,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Employment by branch — same accounts vintage, a different nomenclature habit
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
EMPLOYMENT_FILE = "insee_cn2024_t6208_emploi_par_branche_a38.xlsx"
EMPLOYMENT_SHEET = "T_6208 en niveau"

#: Three A38 branches whose employment row carries an A17 code with a DIFFERENT
#: letter, because at A17 each is a single-branch aggregate with its own label.
#:
#: The table is hierarchical: a branch is written at the coarsest level where it
#: coincides with itself, so most rows resolve by suffix — `AZ` appears as `A5_AZ`,
#: `FZ` as `A5_FZ`. These three do not, and matching them by suffix leaves ten
#: branches unmatched with no error: `CA` is `A17_C1`, `CD` is `A17_C2`, `CL` is
#: `A17_C4`. Each is one-to-one with its A38 branch, verified against the labels —
#: not an aggregation being silently spread.
EMPLOYMENT_ALIASES = {"CA": "C1", "CD": "C2", "CL": "C4"}


def employment(branches: tuple[str, ...], year: int = 2023,
               raw: Path | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Domestic employment by branch, in thousands of persons.

    Ordered to match `branches`, so it can be divided into output directly. Raises
    rather than filling a gap: a branch with no employment row would otherwise get a
    coefficient of zero and quietly contribute no jobs to any shock.
    """
    sheet = _sheet((raw or RAW) / EMPLOYMENT_FILE, EMPLOYMENT_SHEET)
    # The year headers are STRINGS in this workbook, not integers — the column would
    # never be found by an int lookup, and the failure reads as "no such year".
    years: dict[int, int] = {}
    for c in range(3, sheet.max_column + 1):
        header = str(sheet.cell(4, c).value or "").strip()
        if header.isdigit():
            years[int(header)] = c
    if year not in years:
        raise TesError(f"employment table has no year {year}; has {min(years)}-{max(years)}")
    column = years[year]

    by_suffix: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in range(6, sheet.max_row + 1):
        code = sheet.cell(row, 1).value
        if not code or "_" not in str(code):
            continue
        by_suffix.setdefault(str(code).strip().split("_", 1)[1], row)

    values, missing = [], []
    for branch in branches:
        row = by_suffix.get(branch) or by_suffix.get(EMPLOYMENT_ALIASES.get(branch, ""))
        if row is None:
            missing.append(branch)
            continue
        values.append(_number(sheet.cell(row, column).value))
    if missing:
        raise TesError(
            f"no employment row for {missing} — matching by code suffix leaves these "
            f"unmatched, and filling them with zero would silently make those branches "
            f"contribute no jobs to any shock"
        )
    return np.array(values)
